normal.name: James Irish
normal.text: It's funny. The only time PC gaming ever ruined a console experience for me was when Resident Evil came out. I was spoiled rotten by Lucasarts games like Day of the Tentacle and Sam & Max Hit the Road. When I heard those old RE1 voice actors, I was a little incredulous.

normal.name: Videopolis
normal.text: PC or Xbox, if it’s PC adjacent, not too expensive and not too wanky. Otherwise, it’ll just be me and my ever increasing collection of old games (plus the upkeep of those damn old consoles).

normal.name: The Mystery Cartridge (Bradley Hall)
normal.text: Shadowrun (SNES) gets you shot before you press Start. Then: who wanted you dead? 💀 Still Essential Play, because talking to people IS the game. Thanks @pauli-kidd.bsky.social for a game that shaped us! www.themysterycartridge.com/2026/08/shad... #Shadowrun #RetroGaming

normal.name: Dominic Tarason
normal.text: In case you missed it yesterday, Dan Remar - prolific Swedish game dev (both solo and as one of the core crew at Ludosity) released one of his bigger free games. A big, sad, non-linear puzzle platformer epic. Gorgeous DOS-style sprites, moody music and interesting writing. I'd pay for this, easily
normal.media: quotes @steamhype.com: Tower of Gold Is a Free DOS-Styled Puzzle Epic Through a Norse Fantasy Realm

normal.name: Emily the Goblingirl 🏳️‍⚧️
normal.text: Does it have a talking cat? Because that was the thing that won me over for DCC. I am a sucker for talking cats. With attitude. Also it was my first encounter with the whole leveling up it’s a video game in a book kind of thing. Which was fun.

normal.name: Alien Bob but also
normal.text: Was really hoping to use the PC version of War Gods as my first fighting game for Bobvember because funny, but neither in a VM or on real hardware will the game itself receive any input from either keyboard or controller, which makes it a little difficult to play. N64 it is, then.

normal.name: Anthony Rios
normal.text: I remember seeing previews about this in Video Games & Computer Entertainment for months. When the game finally came out, they gave it an awful review. Then for months afterward they were printing codes and tips for it. It was my first clue that gaming mags may not quite be on the up and up.

normal.name: Andrew Walsh
normal.text: Next up is “You forget that you are learning because you are playing”! Playful learning in Early Childhood Teacher Education using Snakes and Ladders educational game, from Annette Furnes. doi.org/10.5920/jpa....
normal.media: link card: “You forget that you are learning because you are playing”! Playful learning in Early Childhood Tea…

normal.name: DXT7
normal.text: For 22 years Remar Games making cool small games and their next one is a massive EGA DOS style puzzle/platforming adventure featuring a first person overworld and lots of secrets! The game and its soundtrack were mainly inspired by Equinox for the SNES.

normal.name: Umni
normal.text: backloggd.com/u/_umni_/rev... #Backloggd #N64 This was a really fun throwback. When I was a kid remember feeling like the DK world was so massive. I would just walk around DK Isle just for the fun of it. I wish Nintendo would bring back the other Kongs, they’re so much fun to play as.
normal.media: link card: _umni_'s review of Donkey Kong 64 | Backloggd

normal.name: SEGA City
normal.text: 'SEGA Touring Car Championship' is one of SEGA's lesser known racers. Did you play it's home conversion on Saturn or PC?
normal.media: image: 'SEGA Touring Car Championship' is one of SEGA's lesser known racers. Did you play it's home conversion on Saturn or PC?

normal.name: Natalia Hawthorne Rey
normal.text: I’m constantly in awe of fanfic writers, especially writers w/OCs in video game universes. How much did you know about the world before throwing yourself in like that? How many ‘correct’ details did you look up/research/hunt for first? Or did you just launch w/what you knew in game, lore be damned?
